Thornwire Mesh Beacon#

The Thornwire Mesh Beacon is a self-deploying micro-node array that ejects up to forty-seven semi-autonomous signal relays — each no larger than a thumbnail — across a designated area upon activation. These relays anchor themselves to surfaces using barbed micro-hooks, forming a decentralized mesh network capable of routing encrypted communications through hundreds of independent paths simultaneously. The network self-heals when nodes are destroyed or disabled, rerouting traffic within milliseconds and making it nearly impossible for signal-tracing equipment to identify the origin or terminus of any transmission.

What distinguishes the Thornwire from conventional mesh nodes is its hostile-environment calibration. The relays are coated in a radar-absorbent ceramic compound developed in partnership with Arcturus Defense Solutions, and each node autonomously cycles through seventeen frequency bands to avoid detection sweeps. The beacon unit itself is roughly the size of a closed fist, ruggedized against EMPs with a faraday-wrapped core, and can be thrown, mounted, or buried — activating on impact, timer, or remote trigger.

The Thornwire is the backbone comms solution for insurgent cells, fixers coordinating multi-team operations, and corporate black-site security teams who need deniable communications infrastructure that leaves no central point of failure. Street-level crews prize it for its disposability — once a job is done, a single destruct signal reduces every relay to slag, leaving nothing for forensics teams to recover.

Vantablack Media Chromatic Null Shroud#

The Chromatic Null Shroud is a full-body garment woven from Vantablack Media's proprietary photon-harvesting microfiber, capable of absorbing up to 99.96% of incident visible light across a 180-degree arc. Embedded within the weave are micro-actuated chromophore cells that sample ambient light from the environment and dynamically redistribute it across the garment's surface, rendering the wearer as a near-perfect visual void that blends into low-light backgrounds rather than standing out as a silhouette.

What distinguishes the Chromatic Null Shroud from simpler blackout garments is its passive operation mode — it requires no power cell during static concealment, drawing only trace current from body heat via integrated thermoelectric strips. Active dynamic blending, used during slow movement, consumes roughly 0.4W and can be sustained for six hours on a standard micro-cell. The garment's outer layer is also treated with a radar-diffusing aerogel coating that scatters millimeter-wave sensor returns, making it effective against automated perimeter systems.

Originally developed for Vantablack Media's deep-cover documentary crews operating in contested corporate zones, the Shroud quickly found a secondary market among infiltrators, black-bag operatives, and high-end couriers. Its civilian framing as 'broadcast equipment' has kept it in a regulatory gray zone for years, and Vantablack Media has made no apparent effort to close that loophole.

Vantablack Media Consensual Blind Relay#

The Consensual Blind Relay is a two-party encrypted communication device that functions on a mutual authentication principle — neither party can transmit until both have physically interacted with paired units within a 90-second window. This handshake requirement was originally designed for Vantablack Media's investigative journalism division, where source protection demanded that no communication could be initiated unilaterally or under duress. Each unit generates a one-time cryptographic handshake derived from both users' biometric pressure signatures, creating an encryption key that exists nowhere in either device's memory after the session ends.

The relay itself transmits over a narrow-band compressed audio channel that mimics the acoustic fingerprint of routine data telemetry — the kind of background noise that Meridian 88's mesh infrastructure produces constantly. A conversation between two CBR units looks, to any intercepting system, like a malfunctioning environmental sensor reporting ambient temperature data. Vantablack's engineers spent considerable effort ensuring the mimicry layer holds up against the city's more sophisticated traffic analysis algorithms, and the current firmware version has not been successfully de-anonymized in active testing.

Despite its journalistic origins, the Blind Relay has found a far wider audience. Lawyers conducting privileged consultations, corporate defectors arranging handoffs, and couples conducting affairs in surveilled housing blocks all use variants of the same device. Vantablack officially discontinued the consumer line after regulatory pressure, but the schematics leaked within six months and third-party units now outnumber originals three to one on the gray market.

Vantablack Media Distributed Echo Mesh Kit#

The Distributed Echo Mesh Kit is a field-deployable mesh networking system packaged as a set of twelve adhesive node discs, each approximately the diameter of a coin and 4mm thick. When placed on surfaces throughout a building, tunnel system, or urban block, the nodes self-organize into a low-power mesh network within ninety seconds, creating a private encrypted communications backbone entirely independent of any existing infrastructure. The mesh operates on frequency-hopping spread spectrum in the sub-GHz band, prioritizing wall penetration and range over bandwidth. The resulting network supports voice, text, and low-resolution positional data for up to eight simultaneous users.

Vantablack Media developed the Echo Mesh Kit ostensibly for their field journalism teams operating in communications-denied environments — protest zones, disaster areas, and regions where corporate or state actors have seized control of local networks. The kit's civilian packaging and media-company branding have allowed it to circulate with relatively light regulatory scrutiny despite capabilities that make it extremely useful for operations that have nothing to do with journalism. Each node is designed to be nearly invisible once placed, with a matte surface that accepts paint, dust, and grime naturally.

The mesh has no central node — if any individual disc is found and destroyed, the network reroutes automatically. Full network collapse requires removal of nine or more of the twelve nodes. The discs are designed to be left behind: they are cheap enough to be considered disposable, and they self-wipe after a factory-set duration between 24 hours and 30 days depending on the configuration selected before deployment.

Vantablack Media Hollow Tongue Relay#

The Hollow Tongue Relay is a passive dead-drop infrastructure device disguised as an ordinary piece of urban furniture or commercial detritus — a cracked utility panel, a branded vending machine fascia, a municipal drainage marker. The relay never initiates contact and emits no continuous signal, making it invisible to both passive monitoring grids and active sweep protocols.

Vantablack Media Orphan Signal Cartridge#

The Orphan Signal Cartridge is a single-use broadcast device designed to transmit a compressed data package — message, file, or audio — across a wide-area signal burst that is specifically engineered to be unattributable to any sender. Vantablack Media developed it as a tool for protected-source journalism: a whistleblower or field correspondent can load the Cartridge with content, set a timed or proximity-triggered release, and walk away. When it fires, the burst mimics the signal profile of legacy infrastructure bleed — the kind of ghost transmissions that Meridian 88's aging broadcast towers emit constantly — making the source indistinguishable from decades-old equipment noise.

The Cartridge is physically a small cylinder, roughly the size of a flare, with a single data input port and a mechanical timer ring. It contains no identifying markings and is manufactured from materials that resist forensic analysis — the polymer casing dissolves in water over 48 hours, and the internal components are designed to thermally self-erase after transmission. The broadcast itself is a single, non-repeating burst lasting between 0.3 and 1.2 seconds depending on data load, making it nearly impossible to triangulate with standard direction-finding equipment.

Vantablack markets the Cartridge under a press-freedom framework and has successfully lobbied for its classification as a journalism tool rather than a communications device in several jurisdictions. In Meridian 88, this legal ambiguity has made it a staple not just of journalists but of anyone who needs to get information somewhere without leaving a trail. The secondary market for used — but not yet fired — Cartridges is surprisingly active, since buyers trust the single-use design to mean no prior data contamination.

Vantablack Media Passive Emission Cartography System#

The Passive Emission Cartography System is a compact, non-transmitting surveillance device that builds a three-dimensional map of an environment by passively cataloguing all electromagnetic emissions present — radio frequencies, WiFi-equivalent mesh signals, cellular handshake traffic, Bluetooth-equivalent short-range protocols, and the low-frequency emissions of powered electronic equipment. Rather than actively scanning, the PECS simply listens, feeding a continuous stream of emission data into a spatial reconstruction algorithm that infers the physical layout of a space and the location of active devices within it. Over a dwell time of fifteen to thirty minutes, it produces a probabilistic floor plan accurate enough to identify rooms, corridors, and the approximate positions of networked devices and electronic equipment.

Vantablack's design philosophy is rooted in their media intelligence background — the system was originally developed to map the technical infrastructure of rival broadcast facilities and live event venues without physical access. The PECS produces no emissions of its own, making it essentially invisible to counter-surveillance sweeps that rely on detecting active scanning equipment. Its outputs are rendered as layered cartographic overlays, color-coded by emission type and confidence level, and can be exported to standard tactical display formats. The system cannot penetrate emission-shielded environments, but it excels at revealing the boundaries of shielded zones by mapping where emissions abruptly terminate.

In Meridian 88, the PECS has migrated from Vantablack's corporate intelligence operations into the hands of extraction teams, investigative journalists, and infrastructure saboteurs. Its passive nature makes it legally ambiguous — it receives only, and its operators argue it is no different in principle from a radio receiver. Authorities contest this framing vigorously, particularly when PECS-generated maps are found in conjunction with evidence of physical infiltration.

Vantablack Media Somatic Noise Cloak#

The Somatic Noise Cloak is a wearable signal disruption garment — a full-torso vest and sleeve assembly lined with Vantablack's proprietary Stochastic Emission Fabric, which generates a continuously randomized electromagnetic emission profile that mimics the ambient background noise of Meridian 88's densely saturated wireless environment. Rather than blocking or absorbing signals, the SNC actively broadcasts low-power noise across a broad spectrum, causing the wearer's electronic footprint to dissolve into the city's background chatter. Biometric sensors, passive RFID sweeps, and short-range identity interrogation systems read the wearer as environmental noise rather than a discrete target.

The garment's intelligence layer is a thin-film processor woven into the collar assembly that samples the local EM environment every 200 milliseconds and adjusts the emission profile to match. In high-traffic commercial zones, the SNC produces a denser, more complex noise signature; in quieter industrial or residential areas, it scales back to avoid the paradox of being the loudest silent thing in the room. Vantablack calls this the Ambient Calibration Loop, and it represents the company's most sophisticated application of their media-disruption research to a physical product. The vest is warm, slightly stiff, and has a faint electrical smell that users report fading after several wears.

The SNC was originally developed for Vantablack's own field journalists and embedded documentary crews operating in corporate-controlled zones where press credentials are selectively enforced. Its availability on the open market — at significant cost — reflects Vantablack's philosophy that information freedom is a consumer product. Corporate security contractors have lobbied unsuccessfully to have it classified as prohibited equipment; the current licensing requirement is enforced inconsistently at best.

Vantablack Media Spectral Relay Shroud#

The Spectral Relay Shroud is a wearable signal architecture layered into a thin, flexible garment worn beneath street clothing — typically a vest or collar insert. It operates by fragmenting outgoing transmissions into thousands of microsecond-duration bursts, scattering them across seventeen discrete frequency bands simultaneously before reassembling them at the receiving end via a paired Vantablack decoder unit. The result is a signal profile that, to conventional intercept equipment, resembles nothing more coherent than ambient electromagnetic noise — radio ghost-chatter from old infrastructure, the static hiss of decaying city grid components.

What distinguishes the Shroud from competing signal-scatter systems is Vantablack's proprietary Chromatic Masking Layer, a passive analog component woven into the garment's lining that mimics the EM signature of the wearer's immediate environment. Near a power relay, the Shroud bleeds into the relay's hum. Near a corporate tower, it replicates the tower's passive emissions. This environmental mimicry is not digital — it cannot be patched out or remotely disabled — making the Shroud uniquely resilient against software-based spectrum sweeps.

The Shroud is a tool of journalists, fixers, and mid-tier syndicate coordinators who need persistent, low-detectability communication over extended operational periods rather than brief tactical bursts. Vantablack markets it obliquely through front distributors, framing it as 'signal privacy apparel' for executives concerned about corporate espionage — a fiction that provides useful legal cover while the product finds its true market in Meridian 88's lower precincts.

Vantablack Subvocal Relay Patch#

The Vantablack Subvocal Relay Patch is a skin-adhered communications device roughly the size of a large bandage, worn over the throat or along the jaw. It intercepts the micro-vibrations produced by subvocal speech — the subtle muscular and laryngeal movements that occur when a person 'thinks' words without vocalizing them aloud — translates them into coherent audio through a proprietary neuromuscular signal processing algorithm, and transmits the result as an encrypted voice signal indistinguishable in quality from normal spoken communication. To an outside observer, the wearer appears completely silent, with no visible earpiece or microphone. The receiving end of the transmission is delivered through bone conduction via a secondary micro-patch worn behind the ear or along the jaw's ramus.

The Patch was developed by Vantablack Media's covert communications subsidiary — a division whose existence the corporation officially neither confirms nor denies — and represents a significant advancement over older subvocal technology, which required extensive individual calibration and produced low-fidelity output. The current generation of Patches uses a self-calibrating algorithm that maps each user's unique subvocal signature within approximately ninety seconds of first wear, achieving voice accuracy exceeding 97% without prior setup. The device is single-use by design: the biosignature calibration is locked to the first wearer's neuromuscular profile, and the adhesive substrate degrades after 72 hours of wear, after which the Patch must be discarded.

The Vantablack Subvocal Relay Patch is the communications tool of choice for operators who need to maintain team contact in environments where any visible communications hardware would be immediately suspicious — undercover infiltrations, social engineering operations, high-security social environments. It is also widely used by Meridian 88's security and protection details, where the ability to communicate without visible earpieces is a significant professional advantage. The single-use nature and premium pricing make it a marker of well-funded operations.

Veil-9 Thermoptic Shroud#

The Veil-9 is a full-body garment woven from a proprietary metamaterial lattice developed by Arcturus Defense Solutions. Microscopic hexagonal cells across the fabric's surface sample ambient light data via embedded photodiodes and re-emit it on the opposite side, creating a passable optical camouflage effect that blends the wearer into static or slowly-changing backgrounds. The system draws power from a flexible spine battery integrated into the back panel, offering roughly four hours of continuous active cloaking before requiring a recharge cycle.

What distinguishes the Veil-9 from cheaper imitators is its thermal management layer — a secondary membrane of aerogel composite interwoven with micro-channel coolant tubing that actively redistributes body heat across a wider surface area, reducing the wearer's IR signature to roughly that of ambient architecture. It does not eliminate thermal output entirely, but it smears it into an indistinct warm haze rather than a recognizable human silhouette. Military-grade thermal optics at close range can still identify a user, but standard corporate security sweeps and drone packages typically fail to flag the signature.

The Veil-9 is almost exclusively found in the hands of corporate black-ops units, high-end fixers, and the occasional well-funded freelancer who can stomach the price. On the street it carries a reputation slightly larger than its actual performance warrants — the name 'Veil' has become shorthand in certain circles for any serious cloaking rig, regardless of brand.

Vespid Dynamics Counter-Drone Electronic Warfare Kit CDEW-2#

A portable electronic warfare kit designed to detect, track, and disable hostile drones through signal jamming, GPS spoofing, and direct electromagnetic pulse. The CDEW-2 includes a drone detection radar, a directional jammer that can sever the control link between a drone and its operator, a GPS spoofer that feeds false position data to cause the drone to fly to a designated capture zone, and a focused EMP emitter that can permanently disable drone electronics at up to 50 meters. Vespid sells the kit as defense against their competitors' drone platforms — and their own, for clients who want protection from all aerial threats.

Vespid Dynamics Pheromone Trail Marker PTM-2#

The markers persist on surfaces for 48-72 hours depending on weather conditions.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric Chemoreceptive Dermal Patch#

The Chemoreceptive Dermal Patch is a biosynthetic sensor array worn against the skin — typically on the inner wrist or neck — that detects and identifies airborne chemical compounds by mimicking the molecular binding mechanisms of biological olfactory receptors. Unlike electronic chemical sensors that rely on catalytic reactions or spectroscopic sampling, the CDP uses a matrix of engineered protein receptors derived from Zheng-Dao's proprietary synthetic biology platform, allowing it to detect trace concentrations of target compounds at parts-per-billion sensitivity. The patch communicates detections through a haptic feedback layer that produces distinct vibrational patterns for different compound classes, supplemented by a companion device that provides full chemical identification.

Zheng-Dao's biological approach gives the CDP a sensitivity profile closer to a trained detection animal than to conventional electronic sensors, but without the false-positive rates that plague organic systems. The receptor matrix is tuned at manufacture for one of several mission profiles: a narcotics-detection variant, an explosives and propellant variant, a toxic industrial chemical variant, and a classified variant marketed exclusively to Arcturus Defense Solutions and certain government clients. The patch has a functional lifespan of approximately 72 hours before the protein receptors degrade, after which it must be replaced. Spent patches are biologically inert and disposable.

The CDP was originally developed for customs and contraband interdiction, and it remains standard issue for Meridian 88's port authority inspectors. Its civilian adoption has been slower, partly due to cost and partly due to a persistent cultural unease about wearing a bioengineered organism on one's skin. Among close-protection operatives and private security, however, it has become valued for its ability to detect the chemical signatures of recently fired weapons, certain stimulants used to suppress fear responses in hostile actors, and the off-gassing of specific explosive compounds used in improvised devices.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric Ciliary Mesh Frond#

The Ciliary Mesh Frond is a bio-synthetic mesh network node grown from Zheng-Dao's proprietary piezoelectric cilia substrate — a branching, fern-like structure roughly the size of a hand that adheres to most surfaces and begins passively harvesting micro-vibrations within minutes of deployment. These harvested vibrations are converted into carrier energy that powers a low-footprint, frequency-hopping mesh relay, capable of extending an encrypted network node into areas with no existing infrastructure. The Frond is literally alive in a limited sense: its cilia respond to environmental stimuli, adjusting their resonance frequency to optimize signal routing without active user input.

The device's distinctive property is its near-zero RF emission profile during idle states. Rather than broadcasting continuously, the Frond listens and responds — it activates only when a paired handshake signal passes within range, acting as a silent repeater that leaves almost no trace on passive spectrum scans. Its biological substrate also means it registers as organic matter on most bio-scanners, not electronics, which allows it to pass through checkpoints concealed in plant material, food packaging, or even worn against skin under loose clothing.

Zheng-Dao markets the Frond to corporate field teams for infrastructure-denied environments, but its properties have made it equally popular among resistance cells and insurgent networks in Meridian 88's outer districts. The irony that a Zheng-Dao product underpins much of the anti-corporate mesh in the city's peripheral zones is not lost on anyone — least of all Zheng-Dao's internal security division, which has reportedly been trying to introduce a remote-kill pathway into newer production runs.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric Dermacalm Thermal Liner#

The Dermacalm Thermal Liner is a form-fitting undersuit that uses Zheng-Dao Bioelectric's adaptive thermoelectric mesh to actively suppress the wearer's infrared signature. The suit samples core body temperature through skin-contact thermistors and drives heat laterally through a network of peltier micro-channels, redistributing thermal output across a broad surface area and venting it downward through the soles at a diffused, low-intensity gradient. The result is a wearer whose thermal profile appears, to most IR detection systems, as ambient background noise rather than a human heat signature.

The Liner's distinctive feature is its biological awareness — rather than simply cooling the wearer to a fixed temperature, the mesh continuously adjusts its redistribution pattern based on exertion level, ambient temperature, and the specific IR band profile of detected scanning systems if a compatible threat-receiver module is attached. This adaptive quality means it remains effective during moderate physical activity, where simpler thermal suits tend to bleed heat from joints and the face. A separate insulated balaclava with micro-vent control is sold as an accessory for full facial IR suppression.

Zheng-Dao markets the Liner officially as a medical garment for patients with autonomic thermoregulation disorders, a classification that has kept it out of the most restrictive regulatory tiers. In practice, the medical market represents perhaps fifteen percent of actual sales. The remainder move through gray-market distributors, corporate procurement channels operating under healthcare exemptions, and outright black-market suppliers.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric Dermal Emission Suppressor#

The Dermal Emission Suppressor is a full-body compression underlayer embedded with a dense mesh of bioelectric regulation nodes developed from Zheng-Dao's research into autonomic system intervention. The underlayer interfaces non-invasively with the wearer's skin surface, monitoring galvanic response, localized surface temperature, and sweat gland activity across the body in real time. Using this data, the nodes apply targeted micro-current stimulation and localized thermoelectric cooling to suppress the involuntary physiological signals that thermal imaging, biometric stress sensors, and galvanic scan systems rely upon to detect and profile human presence.

The Suppressor's primary function is thermal: it maintains the wearer's skin surface temperature within 0.3 degrees of ambient environment temperature by dynamically redistributing body heat through a network of thermoelectric channels that terminate at a heat-sink collar worn at the back of the neck. This collar expels accumulated heat as a diffuse low-temperature plume rather than a concentrated body-shaped signature, dramatically reducing the wearer's profile on thermal imaging systems. A secondary function targets galvanic and stress-response suppression — the bioelectric nodes modulate skin conductivity to flatten the stress-response spikes that biometric scanners at corporate checkpoints use to flag persons of interest regardless of their visual identity.

Zheng-Dao markets a civilian variant of the underlying thermoelectric technology as a medical garment for patients with autonomic dysregulation disorders, which provides a plausible cover story for possession. The full Suppressor, however, exceeds medical specifications significantly and requires calibration to the wearer's specific bioelectric baseline — a process that takes approximately two hours and leaves a calibration record in Zheng-Dao's service network that cautious buyers pay considerable sums to have expunged.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric Efferent Suppression Cuff#

The Efferent Suppression Cuff is a rigid polymer band, twelve centimeters wide, applied to a limb proximal to a traumatic injury to interrupt motor nerve conduction in the affected region without interrupting sensory or autonomic signaling. Where a conventional tourniquet manages blood loss through mechanical compression, the Cuff manages neurogenic shock and uncontrolled muscular spasm through targeted bioelectric interference — a low-amplitude pulsed field tuned to the efferent nerve frequencies documented in Zheng-Dao's proprietary human neural atlas. The result is a limb that can no longer generate voluntary or involuntary muscular contraction distal to the Cuff, while retaining circulation and sensation. This is particularly valuable in crush injury and blast trauma scenarios, where involuntary muscular activity in a damaged limb can worsen internal bleeding and complicate extraction.

The Cuff's selective interference profile is its defining engineering achievement. Early-generation nerve suppression devices — some of which still circulate in the outer ring — used broadband electrical interference that suppressed all nerve conduction indiscriminately, creating a limb that was numb, pulseless, and increasingly ischemic. Zheng-Dao's efferent-selective approach, refined across four hardware generations, preserves the autonomic signals that regulate vascular tone, preventing the vasoconstriction that caused ischemic complications in earlier devices. The Cuff can be worn for up to four hours without clinically significant nerve damage in healthy tissue; in compromised tissue, Zheng-Dao recommends two hours and documents the rest as acceptable liability.

The device has a civilian medical license in Meridian 88's mid-ring districts and is standard equipment in Zheng-Dao's own corporate medical facilities. It also has a significant off-label market: the same efferent suppression field that prevents a trauma patient from thrashing through their own injury can, at modified power settings, be used to incapacitate a limb with surgical precision. This application is not discussed in Zheng-Dao's product documentation, but it is discussed extensively in the parts of the city where the Cuff is known as The Quiet.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric Faradaic Breach Stylus#

The Faradaic Breach Stylus is a handheld electrochemical cutting and access tool developed by Zheng-Dao Bioelectric's industrial maintenance division, nominally for servicing sealed bioelectric conduit housings and corroded terminal blocks in humid or submerged environments. The device delivers precisely modulated faradaic current through a tungsten-carbide tip, using electrochemical dissolution rather than heat or mechanical force to breach conductive barriers. Against standard security-grade lock cylinders, hardened cable ties, and low-gauge ferrous barriers, it operates nearly silently and produces no visible light signature.

The Stylus is approximately the size and weight of a large marker pen, which is not coincidental — Zheng-Dao's design team deliberately pursued a form factor that would survive the pocket of a field technician without dedicated carrying equipment. The tip is replaceable and rated for approximately 400 meters of linear cut before degradation becomes significant. An integrated charge indicator runs along one face as a simple three-segment bar, and the device accepts standard Zheng-Dao 9V bioelectric cells as well as the more common aftermarket equivalents.

The gap between its intended application — unseizing corroded industrial hardware — and its actual range of use is wide enough that Zheng-Dao's legal department has reportedly drafted restriction requests to the city licensing board on three separate occasions, each time withdrawing them when sales projections were reviewed. The Stylus sells exceptionally well.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric Galvanic Carapace Shell#

The Galvanic Carapace Shell is a reactive body armor system developed by Zheng-Dao Bioelectric that integrates a layered bioelectric charge matrix beneath a semi-rigid ceramic composite exterior. When the outer shell absorbs kinetic or thermal impact, piezoelectric transducers convert the energy into a directed galvanic discharge across the armor's surface, creating a localized electric shock field that punishes close-contact attackers and disrupts electronic targeting systems in immediate proximity. The charge cycles reset within 1.4 seconds under normal load, providing near-continuous deterrence against melee engagement.

What distinguishes the Carapace Shell from conventional reactive plating is its symbiotic relationship with the wearer's own bioelectric field. Zheng-Dao's proprietary Dermosync calibration layer reads the operator's skin conductivity and autonomic nervous responses, adjusting discharge thresholds to avoid self-harm during perspiration or stress. The outer shell itself has a faintly iridescent, oil-slick finish caused by the conductive polymer mesh just beneath the surface coating — a visual signature that experienced street operators recognize immediately.

Primarily adopted by corporate security details operating in close-quarters environments such as server vaults, executive transit corridors, and bioresearch facilities, the Carapace Shell has also found significant uptake among mid-tier gang enforcers who acquire surplus units through gray-market channels. It is considered both practical armor and a status symbol in certain criminal strata — wearing one signals that you've survived enough encounters to afford real protection.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric Galvanic Terrain Scribe#

The Galvanic Terrain Scribe is a ground-contact environmental sensor that reads the electrochemical properties of soil, concrete, water-saturated materials, and biological substrate to construct detailed subsurface maps of hidden infrastructure, contamination plumes, buried objects, and biological root or mycelial networks. The device works by injecting precisely calibrated micro-current pulses into a surface through a contact probe and measuring the galvanic response — the way electrical current distributes through and returns from the medium — at an array of secondary contact points positioned around the operator. Variations in galvanic response reveal changes in material density, moisture content, conductivity, and chemical composition beneath the surface, which Zheng-Dao's processing algorithms translate into layered subsurface cross-sections.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric designed the GTS for agricultural and environmental monitoring — specifically for mapping contamination spread in industrial accident sites and assessing soil health in large-scale growing operations. The device's biological sensitivity is exceptional: it can distinguish between the galvanic signatures of living root systems, dormant organic matter, fungal networks, and decomposing biological material. This biological discrimination capability was an agricultural necessity that became an unexpected tactical asset. The GTS can locate buried bodies, living individuals in subsurface spaces, and biological concealment systems (living walls, root-based structural elements) that purely physical scanning methods miss entirely.

In Meridian 88's sprawling underground districts — where significant populations live in unofficial subterranean spaces, where criminal infrastructure runs beneath the official city grid, and where contamination from decades of industrial activity creates complex chemical landscapes — the Galvanic Terrain Scribe has found a user base far beyond its agricultural origins. Urban surveyors, tunnel runners, forensic teams, and environmental investigators all rely on it. Zheng-Dao has leaned into this expanded market while carefully maintaining the agricultural framing in regulatory filings.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric Pelagic Scout Drone — 'The Remora'#

The Remora is a semi-autonomous underwater reconnaissance drone developed by Zheng-Dao Bioelectric, designed for operation in Meridian 88's submerged infrastructure — the flooded lower transit levels, the polluted harbor channels, the cistern networks beneath the city's industrial sectors. Its hull is modeled on pelagic fish morphology, using a flexible myomer-composite spine and undulating fin drives rather than propellers, which produces almost no acoustic signature and leaves no propeller wash. The Remora moves through water the way an organism does — sinuous, unhurried, and very difficult to detect.

Zheng-Dao's biological engineering background is visible throughout the drone's design. Its sensor suite mimics the lateral line system of fish — a distributed array of pressure-sensitive nodes along its hull that detect water displacement, vibration, and chemical gradients. This allows the Remora to navigate in zero-visibility water, detect the movement of personnel or vehicles at range, and track chemical plumes to their source. The drone's outer skin is coated in a biofilm layer that absorbs sonar pings rather than reflecting them, making it functionally invisible to standard underwater detection systems. Onboard processing handles autonomous navigation, but the drone can accept real-time operator commands through a low-frequency acoustic tether.

The Remora is used by salvage operators, intelligence contractors, infrastructure saboteurs, and anyone with operational interest in Meridian 88's submerged spaces. The city's flooded lower levels are largely unmapped and unmonitored — a fact that makes the Remora both practically useful and philosophically significant. In a city where every surface is watched, the water beneath it remains dark.

Zheng-Dao Bioelectric Vagal Interrupt Clamp#

The Vagal Interrupt Clamp is a precision neuroelectrical field instrument designed to apply targeted, calibrated electrical stimulation to the vagus nerve, enabling emergency management of life-threatening cardiac arrhythmias, neurogenic shock, and severe autonomic storms — particularly those triggered by cyberware cascade failures or electrostimulant overdose. The device resembles a modified clamp or forceps approximately 20cm in length, with two paddle-contact ends lined with conductive polymer. It is applied externally to the neck at the carotid triangle, where the vagus nerve runs closest to the skin surface, and delivers a precise sub-threshold electrical signal that modulates nerve activity without causing tissue damage.

Zheng-Dao's engineering philosophy is evident in the device's control interface: a single dial with five positions (Suppress / Moderate Suppress / Neutral Monitor / Moderate Stimulate / Stimulate) and a numerical readout showing real-time heart rate and estimated vagal tone. There are no automated modes. Zheng-Dao's bioelectrical division believes that in the critical moments of a cardiac or autonomic emergency, a trained operator making active decisions produces better outcomes than an automated protocol that cannot account for the full clinical picture. The clamp's signal generator is powered by a rechargeable cell good for approximately four hours of continuous use, and the conductive polymer contacts are replaced per-use via a simple swap cartridge.

It is called 'The Undertaker's Thumb' in field medicine circles — a reference to the ancient practice of pressing the carotid to check for life, and a sardonic acknowledgment that the device occupies the boundary between intervention and acceptance.

  • A black-market modification for the Clamp allows it to interface directly with certain neural cyberware models, producing a controllable euphoric dissociation — the modification is spreading through the high-integration community, and the line between medical use and recreational use is dissolving.

Zheng-Dao Heavy Industries Compact Seismic Imager CSI-2#

A portable seismic imaging device that maps underground structures, tunnels, voids, and buried objects by analyzing the propagation of seismic waves generated by a compact thumper unit. The CSI-2 strikes the ground with a calibrated impact and measures the returning echoes from subsurface features, building a 3D model of everything within 50 meters depth. The system can identify tunnels, buried rooms, underground pipes, geological features, and anomalous density variations that might indicate buried containers or bodies.

Zheng-Dao Heavy Industries Emergency Oxygen Generator EOG-2#

A chemical oxygen generator that produces breathable air through an exothermic chemical reaction, providing 2 hours of oxygen in a device the size of a water bottle. The EOG-2 is activated by pulling a pin that initiates a sodium chlorate decomposition reaction, releasing oxygen at a controlled rate through a breathing mask. The device does not require power, has a 10-year shelf life, and operates in any environment including underwater, in toxic atmospheres, and in vacuum. It is emergency life support reduced to its simplest possible form.

Zheng-Dao Heavy Industries Emergency Power Capacitor EPC-5#

A compact supercapacitor that stores a massive electrical charge and can discharge it in a single burst or as sustained power over several hours. The EPC-5 is the size of a canteen and stores enough energy to power a cyberdeck for 48 hours, jump-start a vehicle, or deliver a single 50kW pulse for weapons applications. The capacitor charges from any power source in 15 minutes and can be recharged thousands of times without degradation. Its dual-mode capability — sustained low-power or instantaneous high-power discharge — makes it the most versatile portable power source in Meridian 88.

Zheng-Dao Heavy Industries Emergency Shelter Pod ESP-2#

A self-deploying emergency shelter that expands from a backpack-sized package into a rigid, sealed habitat capable of sustaining one person for 72 hours. The ESP-2 deploys in 10 seconds using a shape-memory alloy frame that springs into a 2-meter pod when released. The shelter includes atmospheric filtration, water recycling, emergency rations, basic medical supplies, and a distress beacon. The pod's shell provides ballistic protection against small arms fire and NBC protection against chemical and biological threats. It is designed for survival in hostile environments — natural disasters, combat zones, contaminated areas — where getting to safety is not possible and waiting for rescue is the only option.

Zheng-Dao Heavy Industries Gecko Ascender GA-4#

A set of gloves and boots incorporating van der Waals force adhesion pads that allow the wearer to climb vertical surfaces and traverse ceilings like a gecko. Each pad contains millions of synthetic setae — microscopic hair-like structures that create molecular adhesion to any smooth surface. The GA-4 supports loads up to 150 kg (wearer plus equipment), and engagement/disengagement is controlled by a peeling motion that breaks the adhesion contact angle. The system works on glass, metal, concrete, and most polymers, but struggles with rough, porous, or wet surfaces where the setae cannot achieve full contact.

Zheng-Dao Heavy Industries Gravity Assist Mobility Pack GAMP-2#

A backpack-mounted graviton emitter that reduces the wearer's effective weight by up to 80%, enabling enormous leaps, controlled descent from heights, and movement speeds that appear superhuman. The GAMP-2 does not provide true flight — it reduces gravity's effect on the wearer rather than generating lift — but a person weighing effectively 20% of their normal mass can jump 5-story buildings, run along walls for short distances, and survive falls that would kill an unassisted person. The pack's graviton emitter draws enormous power and provides only 15 minutes of active weight reduction per charge cycle.

Zheng-Dao Heavy Industries Magnetic Anchor Boot System MABS-2#

Boots with integrated electromagnetic soles that can be activated to anchor the wearer to any ferrous metal surface with up to 200 kg of pull force per boot. The MABS-2 enables walking on steel walls, ceilings, and exterior surfaces of metal structures including ships, industrial facilities, and steel-framed buildings. The electromagnetic engagement is toggled with a foot-flex gesture, and the force can be modulated for walking (light engagement), climbing (medium), or anchoring against blast or wind (maximum). The boots also prevent the wearer from being thrown by kinetic impacts when anchored to a surface, making them useful for heavy weapons operation and vehicle-mounted combat.

Zheng-Dao Heavy Industries Portable Fusion Battery PFB-2#

A backpack-sized fusion battery that provides 5 kW of continuous power output for 30 days from a single deuterium fuel cell. The battery produces no emissions and generates minimal heat, making it undetectable by thermal surveillance. Zheng-Dao developed it for extended field operations where resupply is impractical.

Zheng-Dao Heavy Industries Powered Grapple Launcher PGL-2#

A wrist-mounted pneumatic launcher that fires a grappling hook with integrated motorized winch, allowing rapid vertical or horizontal traversal. The PGL-2 fires a 4-pronged tungsten-carbide hook attached to 50 meters of braided carbon-fiber cable, and the integrated winch motor can lift loads up to 120 kg at 3 meters per second. The launcher uses a compressed gas cartridge for deployment and the winch runs on a high-density capacitor that provides enough power for one full cable retraction before requiring recharge. The system is compact enough to be concealed under a jacket sleeve.

Zheng-Dao Heavy Industries Seismic Sensor Network SSN-3#

A deployable network of ground-mounted seismic sensors that detect and classify movement on and below the surface within a monitored area. Each sensor spike is driven into the ground and detects vibrations from footsteps, vehicles, tunneling activity, and structural settling. The network's AI classifies detected vibrations — distinguishing between a walking person, a running person, a vehicle, and mechanical digging — and provides the count, direction, and speed of detected movement. The system can detect a single person walking at up to 100 meters and a vehicle at up to 500 meters through ground vibration alone.

Zheng-Dao Heavy Industries Thermal Regulation Bodysuit TRB-3#

A body-conforming suit that actively regulates the wearer's skin temperature across a range of -40°C to +60°C ambient conditions, maintaining a comfortable microclimate regardless of external environment. The TRB-3 uses a network of thermoelectric elements woven into the fabric that can both heat and cool, redistributing thermal energy from hot areas to cold ones and venting or absorbing excess energy through conductive patches on the suit's exterior. The suit also suppresses the wearer's thermal signature, making them difficult to detect with thermal imaging — a side effect that has made it popular with operators who need both environmental protection and thermal stealth.
